From 54e97360b44bed6b4399dd3be3d65f392df940fa Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Shuwei Wu <shuwei.wu@mailbox.org>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 20:46:08 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] clk: spacemit: ccu_mix: fix inverted condition in
 ccu_mix_trigger_fc()

Fix inverted condition that skips frequency change trigger,
causing kernel panics during cpufreq scaling.

Fixes: 1b72c59db0ad ("clk: spacemit: Add clock support for SpacemiT K1 SoC")
Signed-off-by: Shuwei Wu <shuwei.wu@mailbox.org>
Reviewed-by: Yixun Lan <dlan@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260305-k1-clk-fix-v1-1-abca85d6e266@mailbox.org
Signed-off-by: Yixun Lan <dlan@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/clk/spacemit/ccu_mix.c b/drivers/clk/spacemit/ccu_mix.c
index 9578366e9746..a8b407049bf4 100644
--- a/drivers/clk/spacemit/ccu_mix.c
+++ b/drivers/clk/spacemit/ccu_mix.c
@@ -73,7 +73,7 @@ static int ccu_mix_trigger_fc(struct clk_hw *hw)
 	struct ccu_common *common = hw_to_ccu_common(hw);
 	unsigned int val;
 
-	if (common->reg_fc)
+	if (!common->reg_fc)
 		return 0;
 
 	ccu_update(common, fc, common->mask_fc, common->mask_fc);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a bug in `drivers/clk/spacemit/ccu_mix.c` by correcting an inverted condition that caused frequency change triggers to be skipped.

**Modifications in each file:**
- **`drivers/clk/spacemit/ccu_mix.c`**: In the function `ccu_mix_trigger_fc()`, the condition `if (common->reg_fc)` is changed to `if (!common->reg_fc)`. This inverts the logic so that the function now returns 0 early only when `reg_fc` is NULL (i.e., the frequency change register is not available), instead of skipping the trigger when the register *is* available.

**Relationships:**
- The single change reverses the effect of the original condition. Previously, the frequency change trigger (`ccu_update`) was incorrectly bypassed when `reg_fc` was valid, leading to a kernel panic during cpufreq scaling. With the fix, the trigger is now performed exactly when `reg_fc` is present, ensuring proper frequency switching and preventing the crash.

Signed-off-by: Shuwei Wu <shuwei.wu@mailbox.org>

 static int ccu_mix_trigger_fc(struct clk_hw *hw)
 {
 	struct ccu_common *common = hw_to_ccu_common(hw);
 	unsigned int val;
 
-	if (common->reg_fc)
+	if (!common->reg_fc)
 		return 0;
 
 	ccu_update(common, fc, common->mask_fc, common->mask_fc);
 
 	return regmap_read_poll_timeout_atomic(common->regmap, common->reg_fc,
 					       val, !(val & common->mask_fc),
 					       MIX_FC_DELAY_US,
 					       MIX_FC_TIMEOUT_US);
 }

Root cause:
`if (common->reg_fc)` caused an early return when the register pointer was valid, skipping the necessary frequency change trigger. This prevented proper clock frequency switching during cpufreq scaling, leading to kernel panics.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
if (common->reg_fc)
    return 0;
Reason:
The condition is inverted. When `common->reg_fc` is non‑NULL (i.e., a valid register pointer), the function returns early, skipping the frequency change trigger and the subsequent polling. This prevents proper clock frequency switching during cpufreq scaling, leading to kernel panics.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (!common->reg_fc)
    return 0;
Reason:
Checking `!common->reg_fc` ensures that the function returns early only when the frequency change register pointer is NULL (i.e., not available). When the pointer is valid, the function proceeds to set the frequency change bit and poll for completion, enabling correct clock frequency transitions.
